scope: Close OPT-009 at its completed negative feasibility and instrument-diagnosis scope, reconcile current lifecycle and roadmap documents, record one closure result, move the existing uncommitted OPT-009 work from local main onto one new local closure branch without changing its base commit, commit only the frozen allowlist once, and create one conflict-free local non-fast-forward merge commit back into unchanged local main after the full offline non-live suite passes.
closure_basis: The read-only audit of the pre-existing LLM cohort found zero evidence-eligible records for held-out novelty-benefit evaluation.

The frozen prospective protocol selected eight primary and four reserve sources without security or outcome inputs, but the completed first two exact-commit families each produced zero eligible OWASP issue groups against the predeclared minimum of eight.
The isolated positive/negative instrument qualification did not pass: the positive produced one schema-valid but citation-invalid result, while the negative correctly produced none.

The final bounded citation diagnosis proved a possible display-prefix mismatch offline but did not reproduce that causal pattern with the provider: the unchanged prompt returned one exact anchor and the clarification degraded to a nonverbatim citation.

No bounded correction is supported. Additional prompt, planner, provider, or source experimentation would expand the protocol post hoc without evidence that the change addresses the observed gate failure.
terminal_interpretation: OPT-009 is closed as not justified and not feasible at the evaluated scope. This is a negative bounded-investigation result, not a universal claim that semantic novelty prioritization can never work. Any future attempt must be proposed as new work with a newly frozen instrument, untouched source cohort, and separate lifecycle identity rather than reopening or tuning OPT-009.
